A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Real2Edit2Real and contain readable main text and complete supplementary material. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison, including relocated and renumbered appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original real-robot policy results across four tasks, height and texture experiments, component ablations, and supplementary Diffusion Policy and data-scaling results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports video-quality comparisons, generation-time analysis and illustrated failure cases.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 8 retain the same reconstruction, spatial editing, robot pose correction, smooth object relocation and conditioned video-generation procedures. KV caching and distillation are suggested as future work, not implemented changes.

E1.justification: Training datasets and the four principal tasks remain unchanged. v2 Figure 16 adds a demonstrated deformable-object failure scenario; articulated-object limitations were already discussed in v1. The new video-quality evaluation uses the existing four tasks.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds GE-Sim as an evaluated video-generation comparator. v1 cited and used GE-Sim as its backbone but did not report this baseline comparison. Existing policy and data-source comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New Section 10.1 introduces conditional image-to-video evaluation using FVD, LPIPS, SSIM and PSNR. Section 10.3 adds time-versus-success comparisons with 8, 16, 32 and 64 GPUs. Existing policy-training and evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds GPU-scaling and generation-time analysis in Figure 14 and illustrated articulated/deformable-object failure cases in Figure 16. Existing component ablations, depth/Canny removal studies and generated-data scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces no repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, confidence intervals or significance tests. Retained plots preserve their reporting practices, and the added evaluations introduce no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New v2 Table 7 reports Ours versus GE-Sim: FVD 352.9 versus 663.4, LPIPS 0.1252 versus 0.2038, SSIM 0.8647 versus 0.7491, and PSNR 22.95 versus 20.41. Timing and failure findings are also added. All retained policy and data-scaling table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1-5, the training losses and mathematical content of Algorithms 1-4 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same framework contributions, 10-50x data-efficiency claim using 1-5 source demonstrations versus 50 real demonstrations, and height/texture editing claims. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v1 attributes articulated-object difficulties to limited training coverage. v2 extends this explanation to deformable objects and associated visual artifacts, and adds a resource-dependent video-generation bottleneck with proposed future acceleration through KV caching and distillation.

D1.justification: v2 documents generation-time curves for 8-64 GPU configurations, extending v1's single 48.6-second episode timing on eight H100 GPUs. Existing implementation details, hyperparameter tables and resource-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 61 cited works are retained. Sections 2 and 7 and the conceptual comparison in Table 4 preserve the existing novelty arguments and research positioning; GE-Sim was already cited.

P1.justification: Changes include localized introduction edits, an additional project-link sentence, a funding acknowledgement, new appendix subsections and a rewritten limitations section. The main narrative and overall section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7 and Figures 14 and 16, resizes Figure 8, and reduces the retained scaling plot to one column. Existing appendix tables and figures are repositioned or renumbered; the retained qualitative panels are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new GE-Sim comparison adds quantitative support for video quality, while timing analysis and illustrated failures clarify computational costs and applicability limits. These improve evidence and transparency around the unchanged method and policy results. The gain is limited because video-evaluation sample counts and detailed timing procedures remain unspecified.
